hints: Start from the definition of pressure as force divided by area, so you need $\text{force}$ in $\text{kg m s}^{-2}$ divided by $\text{m}^2$.
Write force using $F = ma$ to get its base units, then divide by $\text{m}^2$ to find the target $\text{kg m}^{-1} \text{s}^{-2}$ for pressure.
Rewrite each option with mass in $\text{kg}$, length in $\text{m}$ and time in $\text{s}$, and look for the one that leaves $\text{kg}$ on top with $\text{m}$ and $\text{s}^2$ underneath.
walkthrough: Recall pressure $p = F/A$, so its units are units of force divided by units of area in $\text{m}^2$.
Write force in SI base units using $F = ma$: mass in $\text{kg}$ times acceleration in $\text{m s}^{-2}$ gives force in $\text{kg m s}^{-2}$.
Divide by area: $\text{kg m s}^{-2} / \text{m}^2 = \text{kg m}^{-1} \text{s}^{-2}$, which is the target for pressure.
Check the mass expression: $\text{mass}/[\text{length} \times (\text{time})^2]$ becomes $\text{kg}/[\text{m} \times \text{s}^2] = \text{kg m}^{-1} \text{s}^{-2}$.
This matches the pressure units exactly, while the other expressions give different powers of $\text{m}$ and $\text{s}$. This is option C

options.A: Force is $\text{kg m s}^{-2}$ and length $\times$ speed is $\text{m}^2 \text{s}^{-1}$, giving $\text{kg m}^{-1} \text{s}^{-1}$ which has only one power of $\text{s}$ in the denominator.
options.B: Force is $\text{kg m s}^{-2}$ and length $\times$ time is $\text{m s}$, giving $\text{kg s}^{-3}$ which does not match pressure.
options.C: Mass divided by length $\times$ (time)$^2$ is $\text{kg m}^{-1} \text{s}^{-2}$, which is identical to the SI base units of pressure.
options.D: Mass $\times$ (time)$^2$ divided by length gives $\text{kg s}^{2} \text{m}^{-1}$, with time in the numerator instead of the denominator.
